question.text: Will any North American country have a CDC travel advisory issued in November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if a country in North America has a Travel Health Notice (THN) by the Centers for Disease Control at its [THN](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices) page newly issued in November 2026.
question.fine_print: No other resolution source will be used in resolving this question.

research:
As of the morning of November 1, 2026, the CDC notices page shows no North American notice issued in November. The most recent "New" one is still Hepatitis A in Costa Rica (September 18, 2026). The current Ebola entry rule targets the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), not North America. Over the past year, new North American notices have appeared roughly every two months, with about five in 2026 so far.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-01: I read the [CDC notices page](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices) and its [RSS feed](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/rss/notices.xml) directly. The page footer says "Page last reviewed: October 19, 2026." Nothing on the page or in the feed is dated after October 19, 2026. The newest items are Ebola (Bundibugyo strain) in Kenya, Level 1, labelled "New" on 2026-10-19, and two yellow fever notices (Ghana "New", Colombia "Updated") on 2026-10-16.
- North American notices currently on the page:
  - Hepatitis A in Costa Rica: "New", 2026-09-18
  - Chikungunya in Nicaragua: "Updated", 2026-09-03
  - Chikungunya in Costa Rica: "Updated", 2026-07-30
  - Diphtheria in Haiti: "New", 2026-06-25
  - Hepatitis A in Canada (Manitoba): "New", 2026-06-04
  - Rocky Mountain spotted fever in Mexico: 2025-12-23
- Multi-country notices that include North American countries:
  - Global Dengue: "Updated", 2026-10-02. Its list includes Costa Rica, Cuba and Panama.
  - Global Measles: 2025-05-28.
- Ambiguity: it is not clear whether adding a North American country to a multi-country notice like Global Dengue, or "Updating" an existing notice, would count as "newly issued." The page marks items as either "New" or "Updated," which may matter for resolution.

## 2. Current status
- 2026-11-01: Nothing has settled the question yet. I found no North American notice dated November 2026.
- 2026-10-30 and 31: News stories about the CDC's new Ebola attestation, effective 2026-11-03 at 11:59 p.m. EST, describe a rule for passengers flying into the US who were in the DRC. It is not a Travel Health Notice for any North American country. ([Clarín](https://www.clarin.com/sociedad/nuevo-requisito-obligatorio-poder-ingresar-via-aerea-estados-unidos-partir-martes_0_vmCh4L3NFa.html), [MoneyTalksNews](https://www.moneytalksnews.com/you-wont-be-allowed-to-fly-into-the-us-without-signing-this/), [Prensa Libre](https://www.prensalibre.com/guatemala/comunitario/nuevo-formulario-para-viajar-a-estados-unidos-tres-puntos-clave-sobre-su-vigencia-presentacion-fisica-o-digital-y-que-pasa-si-no-lo-lleva/))

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-30: The CDC widened the Ebola boarding declaration to all passengers and crew flying into the US. ([RusTourismNews](https://www.rustourismnews.com/2026/10/30/new-us-flight-rule-from-november-3-now-applies-to-all-passengers-and-crew/))
- 2026-10-19: CDC issued a new Level 1 notice for Ebola in Kenya. This shows CDC is still issuing new notices. ([CDC](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices))
- 2026-10-13: According to search results, CDC's dengue page lists notices for Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Honduras, Jamaica and Mexico, and says Cuba entered the high-transmission category on 2026-10-07. That differs from the dengue country list I saw on the notices page, so it needs checking. ([CDC dengue](https://www.cdc.gov/dengue/areas-with-risk/index.html))
- 2026-09-03: CDC's chikungunya page lists Mexico among places with an outbreak notice, according to search results. I could not confirm this on the notices page. ([CDC chikungunya](https://www.cdc.gov/chikungunya/data-maps/index.html))
- I found no specific new outbreak news from October 2026 in North America. A report of cyclospora in travelers returning from Mexico looks like it dates from 2025. ([LBC](https://www.lbc.co.uk/world-news/mexico-hotels-explosive-diarrhoea-parasite/))

## 4. Base rates
- North American notices first issued as "New" over roughly the last 14 months (Nicaragua's and Costa Rica's chikungunya notices are left out because their original "New" dates are unknown):
  - 2025-09-18: Oropouche in Cuba, Level 1 ([CDC Cuba page](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/destinations/clinician/none/cuba))
  - 2025-09-26: Chikungunya in Cuba, Level 2 (same source)
  - 2025-12-23: Rocky Mountain spotted fever in Mexico
  - 2026-06-04: Hepatitis A in Canada
  - 2026-06-25: Diphtheria in Haiti
  - 2026-09-18: Hepatitis A in Costa Rica
- Possibly more: chikungunya in Costa Rica and Nicaragua were probably first issued in 2026, but I could not find their original dates.
- That makes roughly 6 to 8 new North American notices in about 14 months, an average of about 0.4 to 0.6 a month. They are clustered, though: none appeared from January to May 2026. My rough estimate is that about 35 to 50% of recent months had at least one. I could not reach CDC's archive of past notices (the URLs I tried returned 404 errors), so this count may be incomplete.
- Over the past month, CDC has issued new notices for other regions (Ghana on 10-16, Kenya on 10-19), so it is still issuing new notices.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on CDC Travel Health Notices. The Kalshi markets supplied are about State Department travel advisories (for example a Taiwan Level 4 at 0.02 before 2027, and downgrades for Uganda and the DRC). They are a different system and not relevant here.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- November is the end of the Atlantic hurricane season (it closes November 30). A major storm in the region could prompt a disaster-related notice.
- Dengue and chikungunya transmission is still active in the Caribbean and Central America. Cuba's dengue status reportedly rose on 2026-10-07, so it could get its own notice or an addition to the global dengue notice.
- The Ebola outbreak in the DRC and Uganda, with a linked case in Kenya, could spread through imported cases. A new North American notice from that is unlikely but possible.
- Existing North American notices (chikungunya, hepatitis A, Haiti diphtheria) are more likely to get "Updated" than to have new ones issued. Updates may not count.

## Will a North American country get a new CDC Travel Health Notice in November 2026? Research notes

As of the forecast close, nothing settles the question. The last new notice for a North American country was Hepatitis A in Costa Rica on 2026-09-18. In the past 13 months, a new notice was issued in about 5 or 6 of those months.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-19 ("Page last reviewed" date): I read the [CDC THN page](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices) directly. It lists these notices for North American countries:
  - New: Hepatitis A in Costa Rica, 2026-09-18
  - New: Diphtheria in Haiti, 2026-06-25
  - New: Hepatitis A in Canada (Manitoba), 2026-06-04
  - Rocky Mountain spotted fever in Mexico, 2025-12-23
  - Updated, Level 2: Chikungunya in Nicaragua (2026-09-03) and Chikungunya in Costa Rica (2026-07-30)
  - Global Dengue, Level 1, updated 2026-10-02: covers Costa Rica, Cuba and Panama
- The page's newest entries are Ebola Bundibugyo in Kenya (New, Level 1, 2026-10-19) and Yellow Fever in Ghana and Colombia (2026-10-16). Neither is a North American country.
- I found no CSV, JSON or RSS data file behind the page. It is plain HTML.
- Wording risk: the page labels entries "New" or "Updated". The question says "newly issued", and its background refers to the "most recent new notice", which suggests only "New" entries count. It is unclear whether adding a North American country to a multi-country notice (such as Global Dengue) would count.

### 2. Current status
- 2026-10-31: There is no new North American notice since Costa Rica Hepatitis A on 2026-09-18. Nothing has happened that settles the question.
- 2026-10-30/31: The news items about a mandatory CDC Ebola declaration for US-bound flights (effective 2026-11-03) are an entry-requirement order about the DRC. They are not a THN for a North American country, even though Guatemalan and Salvadoran outlets covered it. [Prensa Libre](https://www.prensalibre.com/guatemala/comunitario/nuevo-formulario-para-viajar-a-estados-unidos-tres-puntos-clave-sobre-su-vigencia-presentacion-fisica-o-digital-y-que-pasa-si-no-lo-lleva/), [Rustourismnews](https://www.rustourismnews.com/2026/10/30/new-us-flight-rule-from-november-3-now-applies-to-all-passengers-and-crew/)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-20: Canada's public health agency (PHAC) updated its chikungunya notice covering Costa Rica, Cuba, French Guiana, Nicaragua and Suriname. CDC's current page has no Cuba chikungunya notice, so CDC could add one. [PHAC](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/health-safety/travel-health-notices)
- 2026-10-13: According to search summaries of CDC's dengue page (I did not open it), Cuba meets the criteria for "high transmission" and had 10 or more cases among travelers in the last three months. [CDC dengue](https://www.cdc.gov/dengue/areas-with-risk/index.html)
- 2026-09-03: CDC updated the Nicaragua chikungunya notice. It was first issued 2026-08-03; sources disagree on whether it started at Level 1 or Level 2. [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322990/20260804/cdc-issues-nicaragua-chikungunya-alert-suspended-vaccine-leaves-us-travelers-one-choice.htm), [CDC](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/chikungunya-nicaragua)
- 2026-07-16 (one secondary source; coverage starts around 07-21): CDC issued the Level 2 Costa Rica chikungunya notice. [Tico Times](https://ticotimes.net/2026/07/31/cdc-costa-rica-chikungunya-travel-notice-update)

### 4. Base rates
New CDC notices for North American countries I could identify in the past 13 months:
- about 2025-09-30: Cuba chikungunya, Level 2 (since removed). [Diario Las Américas](https://www.diariolasamericas.com/america-latina/eeuu-emite-alerta-chikungunya-cuba-n5383359)
- 2025-12-23: Mexico, Rocky Mountain spotted fever
- 2026-06-04: Canada, Hepatitis A
- 2026-06-25: Haiti, diphtheria
- about 2026-07-16: Costa Rica, chikungunya
- 2026-08-03: Nicaragua, chikungunya
- 2026-09-18: Costa Rica, Hepatitis A

That is about 7 notices across roughly 6 of the 13 months (Sep 2025, Dec 2025, Jun, Jul, Aug and Sep 2026). There were dry stretches of Oct to Nov 2025 and Jan to May 2026, and October 2026 also had none. The list may be incomplete, because I could not find an archive of retired notices (the /archive URL returns a 404). Notices issued and later retired could be missing.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on CDC travel notices. The Kalshi markets supplied are about State Department travel advisories (Uganda, DRC, Taiwan and others) or unrelated topics, so they do not match this question.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution (2026-12-01)
- Mosquito-borne disease is still active in the Caribbean and Central America: Cuba chikungunya and dengue (PHAC has notices, CDC has no chikungunya notice), and chikungunya in Nicaragua and Costa Rica. A new country-specific notice for Cuba, or an outbreak elsewhere, would count. [PHAC](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/health-safety/travel-health-notices)
- Atlantic hurricane season ends 2026-11-30. CDC rules allow notices for natural disasters. I did not check whether any November storm is likely.
- The Ebola response is taking up CDC attention: Level 4 in DRC, a new Level 1 for Kenya on 10-19, and the 11-03 boarding attestation. This could affect how much the travel-notice team does elsewhere; this is my inference, not a sourced claim.
- Watch for newly issued Global Dengue or Global Measles updates that add North American countries. Whether those count is unclear (see section 1).

Sources: [CDC THN page](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices), [CDC dengue areas](https://www.cdc.gov/dengue/areas-with-risk/index.html), [CDC Nicaragua chikungunya](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/chikungunya-nicaragua), [CDC Costa Rica chikungunya](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/chikungunya-costa-rica), [PHAC notices](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/health-safety/travel-health-notices), [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322990/20260804/cdc-issues-nicaragua-chikungunya-alert-suspended-vaccine-leaves-us-travelers-one-choice.htm), [Tico Times](https://ticotimes.net/2026/07/31/cdc-costa-rica-chikungunya-travel-notice-update), [Diario Las Américas](https://www.diariolasamericas.com/america-latina/eeuu-emite-alerta-chikungunya-cuba-n5383359), [Prensa Libre](https://www.prensalibre.com/guatemala/comunitario/nuevo-formulario-para-viajar-a-estados-unidos-tres-puntos-clave-sobre-su-vigencia-presentacion-fisica-o-digital-y-que-pasa-si-no-lo-lleva/), [Rustourismnews](https://www.rustourismnews.com/2026/10/30/new-us-flight-rule-from-november-3-now-applies-to-all-passengers-and-crew/), [CBS News Cuba](https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/news/mosquito-borne-illnesses-cuba-chikungunya-dengue)

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 30 days remain, until around 2026-12-01. Yes requires a CDC Travel Health Notice for a North American country (the background treats Central America and the Caribbean as North American) that is newly issued in November 2026 on the CDC notices page. It is unclear whether "Updated" notices count. A strict reading needs a "New" label.

(b) Status quo: no North American notice dated November exists yet. The last "New" one was Hepatitis A in Costa Rica on Sept 18. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

(c) Base rate: about 6 to 8 new North American notices in 14 months, roughly 0.4 to 0.6 per month. They are clustered, so about 35 to 45% of months had at least one. A Poisson model with λ≈0.5 gives about 39%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - CDC is still issuing new notices actively (Kenya on Oct 19, Ghana on Oct 16).
  - Dengue and chikungunya activity in the Caribbean and Central America is ongoing, and Cuba's dengue level reportedly rose on Oct 7.
  - Hurricane season runs to Nov 30.
  - If updated notices count, the chance is considerably higher, since North American notices are updated frequently.
- For No:
  - Nothing has been posted since Oct 19, and no specific North American outbreak news emerged in October 2026.
  - New North American notices often go months without one (none from January to May 2026).
  - November is a lower season for arboviruses in the northern part of the region.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: CDC posts updates to existing chikungunya or dengue notices, or none at all, and no new North American country notice appears.
- Yes: CDC issues a new Level 1 notice, for example dengue in Cuba, measles in Mexico or Canada, or a post-hurricane notice for a Caribbean nation, in mid-November.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 38%. I move slightly up because of resolution ambiguity: an update could plausibly count as "issued". I move slightly down for the quiet October news and the seasonal decline. These roughly cancel, leaving about 38%.

Probability: 38%
